issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch: the problem statement and UML specify a public SealSaloon(String) constructor (constructor takes the saloon name), but both the template code (Main.java) and the solution implement a no-argument constructor (public SealSaloon()). This contradicts the specification and can confuse students about whether they must implement a constructor that accepts a name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent: either update the template and solution to provide public SealSaloon(String name) (and adapt usages), or change the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument constructor. Preferable fix: implement public SealSaloon(String name) in the template/solution and reflect this in the Main test code and UML.

issues.description: Contradiction about stock initialization: the problem text instructs that the Stock (final stock) should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor, while later notes require the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing an instance-shared static field 'in the constructor' is contradictory. The solution resolves this by declaring and initializing a static final Stock at field declaration, but the problem statement's guidance is inconsistent and may mislead students.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intent in the problem statement: if stock must be shared across all SealSaloon instances, state that it should be a static (and possibly final) field initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Alternatively, if stock should be per-instance, remove the requirement that stock is static. Update the UML/text accordingly so initialization instructions and static/shared requirement are consistent.

issues.description: The problem specification and UML require a SealSaloon constructor SealSaloon(String) (the saloon name) and mention storing the saloon name, but the provided Solution implements a parameterless constructor (public SealSaloon()) and the Template's commented Main invokes new SealSaloon() with no argument. This mismatch in the constructor signature / presence of a saloon name field creates confusion about whether students must implement a name parameter and a corresponding field/getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the Solution and Template to provide and use a constructor SealSaloon(String name) and store a private final String name with a public getter, or (B) modify the problem statement and UML to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and remove the explicit saloon name requirement. Preferred fix: implement public SealSaloon(String name) in SealSaloon, store the name as a private final field, and update any usages (e.g., Main) to call new SealSaloon("SaloonName").
